question: Should OpenClaw accept `channels.msteams.accounts` and `channels.msteams.defaultAccount` as the public Microsoft Teams multi-account contract, with legacy root config as the implicit default and enabled named accounts requiring explicit identity plus webhook port?
rationale: This PR changes public operator config, auth selection, setup, and persistent Teams routing state, so implementation review can verify coherence but should not choose the permanent Teams product contract.

options.title: Accept the account-map contract
options.body: Approve this PR's account map, default-account fallback, named-account identity rules, and per-account webhook ports as the intended Teams multi-account model.

options.title: Revise before merge
options.body: Ask for changes to the config shape, setup prompts, or listener model before making the contract public.

options.title: Pause for separate design
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers prefer shared-route multiplexing or another Teams account ownership model first.

recommendation.title: Accept the account-map contract
recommendation.body: Approve this PR's account map, default-account fallback, named-account identity rules, and per-account webhook ports as the intended Teams multi-account model.

likelyOwner.reason: BradGroux is explicitly asked for Microsoft/Teams guidance in the PR discussion and has recent Teams-area history in the affected config/runtime surface.
